newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Vanguard upbeat on migraine drug.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Vanguard upbeat on migraine drug.

text.p: Fledgling British drug company Vanguard Medica Group Plc said on Monday it expected to submit its migraine drug, VML 251, for regulatory approval at the beginning of 1999.

"We expect to to be putting in a regulatory application at the beginning of 1999, after that it depends on what the FDA thinks of it," Robert Mansfield, chief executive of Vanguard Medica, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Vanguard said earlier that clinical study results were encouraging and added that SmithKline Beecham Plc had confirmed it would take up the worldwide marketing of VML 251.
The company, floated on the stock exchange in May, said that on the basis of its phase IIb clinical studies it planned to commence phase III clinical trials in January 1997.

Vanguard raised 46.4 million stg at the floatation to fund its pipeline, which includes migraine and kidney drugs with VML 251 estimated by analysts to account for around half of Vanguard's current stock market valuation.

By 0935 GMT, shares in Vanguard had surged 57-1/2p to 567-1/2 on the back of the announcement. The drug firm revealed in September that its pretax loss for the six months to June widened to 3.7 million stg from 1.8 million previously.

Vanguard, which has a cash position of just over 50 million stg, will receive a series of milestone payments and, upon commercialisation of VML 251, a share of net operating receipts on a worldwide basis.

"There are five milestone payments and we are just about to receive the first one which is about one million dollars, that is really to signify SmithKline's intention to market this compound," Mansfield told Reuters.
A further four payments are due when Vanguard submits the drug in the U.S. and Europe and then when it gets approval in the U.S. and Europe.
Vanguard was unable to disclose what it expected to receive upon commercialisation of the drug.
"It is a substantial reward for our efforts in development, was all that Mansfield would say.
Given the size of the market -- some six percent of men and 14-18 percent of women suffer from migraine -- it was obviously a "very large market," said Mansfield.
He said that Glaxo Wellcome Plc was selling around 700 million stg a year of its anti-migraine compound Imigran.
"There was a certain amount of dissatisfaction prior to the introduction of Imigran with exisiting treatments, so I suspect this is going to be a very big market in the future." he said.
Mansfield said the company was working on four other compounds and was looking at further new compounds to bring into the company's portfolio.
